newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP copper unit reports year A$8 mln loss.
newsitem.headline: BHP copper unit reports year A$8 mln loss.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co ltd said on Friday its copper division posted a loss of A$8 million, including abnormal items, for the 1996/97 financial year ending May 31 versus a profit of A$643 million the previous year.
Excluding abnormal items, the 1996/97 result was A$542 million, down A$36 million or 6.2 percent year-on-year, BHP said.

"The situation in the North American mining activities was that operational difficulties during the year increased costs, producing results below earlier expectations and this has been aggravated by lower copper prices for much of the period," BHP said.
At the San Manuel, Arizona complex, production was affected for several months in the original orebody and by delays in commissioning the new Lower Kalamazoo orebody.
Production at the Tintaya mine in Peru and Robinson mine in the U.S. was better in the last quarter and cost saving initiatives are underway in all areas of copper's operations.
Sales revenue for the year was A$3.8 billion, 28 percent above last year, BHP said.

The increase was due to inclusion of the former Magma operations and increased shipments from the Escondida mine in Chile, partly offset by lower Ok Tedi shipments from Papua New Guinea and lower average copper prices, BHP said.
Copper prices, which were depressed for most of the first half of the year, partially recovered in the past six months, the company noted.
The average price booked for copper shipments in the year was US$1.06 per pound versus US$1.18 the previous year, BHP said.
Unhedged copper shipments not finalised as of May 31 1997 have been brought to account at US$1.10 per pound, BHp said.
The London Metal Exchange copper spot price at 30 May 1997 was US$1.18 per pound, compared to US$1.15 per pound at 31 May 1996.
For the year to May 31, 1998, 16 percent of projected copper sales are covered by put options at an average price of US$0.89 a pound, BHP said.
For the same period, 16 percent of projected copper sales are covered by forward contracts at an average price of US$1.01 a pound, BHP said.
BHP is the world's second largest producer of copper.

BHP on Friday posted an overall 1996/97 net profit of A$410 million after abnormal losses of A$976 million, compared with A$1.046 billion a year earlier, which followed abnormal losses of A$247 million. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
